A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LfCD-GRIP research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between appendix sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original navigation and manipulation simulations, ablations, and real WidowX robot experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and real-robot results and adds time-penalty comparisons and hyperparameter sensitivity results in Appendices H–I.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the proximity objectives, confidence estimation, interpolation, masking, and network architectures remain unchanged. Section 4.2 newly specifies the confidence threshold as the maximum expert-state variance, updated each iteration; this fills an earlier documentation gap without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MiniGrid-LfCD, Maze2D, FetchPick, FetchPush, and WidowX-Pick. Section 5.4 changes the severity-study environment from FetchPick to FetchPush while Figure 6 retains the same plotted results. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects a label or changes the evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds Expert performance to the quantitative comparisons in Figures 4, 5, and 8; Expert already appeared in the severity comparison in v1. Appendix H also evaluates three time-penalty variants of Proximity. The existing BC, GAIL, GAIfO, SSRR, Proximity, and Proximity-Drop comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added analyses introduce time-penalty magnitudes of 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001, Maze2D demonstration-size sweeps, and MiniGrid sweeps over pretraining iterations, temporal decay, and Monte Carlo sample count. These are additional experimental protocols; the original Table 2 settings and main evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H tests whether a simple time penalty can substitute for interpolation, while Appendix I investigates sensitivity to demonstration quantity, pretraining, temporal decay, and confidence-estimation samples. These substantially expand mechanism and robustness checks beyond the retained masking, action-use, severity, and training-curve analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report four random seeds and retain the existing error-bar and shaded-band reporting practices. Tables 4–5 provide point estimates without introducing new significance tests, confidence intervals, or revised run counts. Varying Monte Carlo samples within the model is an experimental parameter sweep, not additional independent evaluation runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds Expert scores and substantive control and sensitivity outcomes. Table 4 reports Maze2D episode lengths of 101 for LfCD-GRIP, 112 for Proximity, and 119/111/112 for the penalty variants; Table 5 reports MiniGrid length increasing from 25.2 to 33.5 when pretraining changes from 2 to 10 iterations. Figure 8 also revises the BC and LfCD-GRIP simulation bars. The real-robot 100-second versus 12-second result and Figure 10 training curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, action-space relationship, objectives, confidence formula, and interpolation mathematics are retained. Section 3 elaborates the goal-reaching assumption already reflected in v1's method and limitations. The new time-penalty discussion supplies informal reasoning rather than new formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three listed contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims about learning beyond constrained demonstrations through state-only proximity interpolation. The added future-work framing develops the partial-coverage motivation already discussed in v1 Appendix F without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds explanations involving early-failure incentives, uniform transition penalties, and penalty-scale interactions with learned rewards. Appendix I identifies sensitivity to excessive pretraining and small Monte Carlo sample counts. The conclusion expands the broader partial-coverage interpretation, while v1's explanation about initially non-goal-directed PPO rollouts is removed. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the dynamic confidence threshold, discloses MiniGrid's fully observable 19×19×4 input, and states that supplementary source code includes README commands for all experiments. Code availability cannot be verified from these PDFs. Existing architectures and Table 2 are retained, but the appendix paragraph defining training-curve aggregation over successful paths and its failure fallback is removed.

R1.justification: V2 removes the SAIL citation by Arachchige et al. (2025) and the deterministic-policy-gradient citation by Jain et al. (2025). Appendix G and Table 3 elaborate the existing contrast with T-REX, D-REX, and SSRR, particularly action-space and demonstration-quality assumptions. The overall related-work organization remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized prose and author/header edits, expands the formulation and confidence explanations, and adds Future Work, Reproducibility Statement, and LLM Usage sections. Existing architecture/training appendices move after the masking and training-curve appendices. Most main-text wording and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4, 5, and 8 gain Expert bars and revised legends. Figure 6 is relocated and its Expert color changes; Figures 9–10 are resized or rearranged. Tables 3–5 are added and Table 2 moves with its appendix. The principal diagrams and real-robot imagery remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reproducibility and empirical assessment through the explicit confidence threshold, direct Expert comparisons, and new mechanism and sensitivity checks. These gains are limited by reporting defects: the stated 12.5% dataset experiment lacks a Table 5 result, and Appendix I's claim that all MiniGrid baselines exceed 32 steps conflicts with Figure 4. The additions strengthen scrutiny of the retained method, but their inconsistencies prevent a substantial overall improvement.
